grand_strategy.reading:
Syria under Ahmed al-Sharaa runs the grand strategy of a victorious insurgency
that has to become a state before its patrons lose patience. The rank order of the
objectives is the order of the dangers: first the monopoly of force (the SDF
deal, Suwayda, the coast), then legitimacy (delistings, sanctions relief, Caesar
repeal), then money. The method is multi-alignment at the leader level, with no
patron allowed to own the state: Turkey for the army, the Gulf for the cash,
Washington for the permission to trade, Russia kept only as a training partner,
Iran expelled. The Luttwak pattern is that each move that builds the state
also invites an outsider into it: the Turkish umbrella draws the Israeli strike,
the conquest of the east takes away the American cover, the pressure on
minorities supplies the conditions that Western money carries. Signals that are
not rows: the Syrian army's deployment to the Lebanese border in March 2026,
al-Sharaa's refusal to attend the 2025 Baghdad summit, and Egypt's refusal of a
Syrian ambassador. Open question for the next review: whether the 25 Aug SDF
dissolution survives its first test in Hasakah and Kobani, and whether an
Israeli security agreement is signed or the south settles into a frozen
occupation. Not read in this pass: Crisis Group and Carnegie analyses of 2026
(the search budget ran out), so grades on Israel, Russia and China rest on press
and official statements.
